claim: Number of LNPs actually injected per screen
locus_A: Main text: 'Of the 24 cationic LNPs we formulated, 23 met our 200 nm and single DLS peak selection criteria'; 59 of 64 neutral; 55 of 56 anionic; 137 in total
locus_B: Fig S6 tables, counted by horizontal rule detection on the rasters (not by eye): cationic 25 rules -> 24 bands -> 22 LNP rows; anionic 53 -> 52 -> 50; neutral 61 -> 60 -> 58. Total 130.
what_we_emitted: Nothing. No per-LNP pooled value is emitted.
why: Seven pooled LNPs are stated in the text but absent from the tables. The deficit is INDEPENDENTLY VISIBLE in the arithmetic: the cationic table's lung, liver and spleen share columns sum to 97.364, 89.527 and 93.450 instead of 100, all short in the same direction, and the three shortfalls average to 6.5528 which equals the 'average' column's own shortfall to 3.3e-10. One missing pooled LNP accounts for the cationic case exactly.

claim: The lead LNP of a screen is its best performer
locus_A: Main text: 'Predictions made by high-throughput in vivo screens should be confirmed using individual LNPs. Thus, we characterized a lead LNP from each library.' Fig S6 caption: 'The lead LNPs ... are shown in the red boxes.'
locus_B: Fig S6c, cationic: the red vector stroke (colour exactly (1,0,0), 1.25 pt, SI p.17 y=[221.1,230.7] pt) sits on the 10th data row = LNP #11 (DDAB, C14PEG2K, 35/18/2.5/44.5), which is Cat-LNP. LNP #11 ranks 2 of 22 on BOTH the Lung average column (10.708 vs LNP #2 at 12.563) and the average normalized delivery column (7.065 vs 8.163).
why: 'Lead' is never defined in the paper. The chosen cationic lead is not the argmax of either column of its own screen table. This matters for the project's open question on whether benchmark or lead compounds top their screens: here the selected lead does NOT.

claim: Fig S2b row N3 is DOPC
locus_A: Fig S2b caption and Name column: 'DOPC'. The main text and every reference define DOPC as 1,2-dioleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine, a DIESTER.
locus_B: The structure drawn in Fig S2b row N3, read at 1.6x zoom: the sn-1 chain terminates in a bare oxygen bonded to the glycerol CH2 with NO carbonyl, while sn-2 carries a normal ester. As drawn that is 1-O-oleyl-2-oleoyl-PC, an ether/ester mixed species, not DOPC. Every other diacyl lipid in the same panel (N4-N8) is drawn with two carbonyls.
what_we_emitted: Nothing. DOPC is not a component of any emitted formulation.
why: A probable drawing error in a catalogue panel. Flagged, not corrected: a name-versus-structure disagreement is a question for the authors, and the AC_2025 precedent is that repairing the wrong half puts measurements on wrong molecules. Evidence level: read from a 219.8 dpi raster at 1.6x; not re-derived by vector geometry, because the page carries 0 vector paths.

locus_A: Fig S13a Lung, Liver, Kidney, Spleen, Heart and Fig S13b Lung, Liver, Kidney, Heart all draw stubs at 0, 20, 40, 60, 80 and 100.

claim: Fig S13 and Fig S15 might not plot the same experiment
locus_A: Fig S13 plots 'tdTom+ Cells (%)' with a PBS bar beside every LNP bar, over five organs, in the order ECs/Monocytes/DCs/T/B for lung. Fig S15 plots 'tdTom+ Cells (%), above background' with no PBS bar, over three organs, in the order ECs/DCs/T/B/Monocytes for lung.
locus_B: Joined on the LABEL, not the column index: over the 14 cell types readable in both, Fig S13 raw minus Fig S15 above-background lies in [-0.361, +3.839] percentage points with median 0.635, and 14 of 14 fall inside the 0-4.5% PBS band that Fig S13 itself draws.
what_we_emitted: The Fig S13 raw values only; Fig S15 is marked inadmissible in 05_values.csv as the same measurements in a second normalisation.
why: RETIRED. The two figures are the same experiment, S15 = S13 minus its PBS control, and the differing cell-type ORDER is a drawing choice. Had the join been on column index instead of label, lung Monocytes would have been compared against lung DCs.

claim: The C10 anchors might be copies of the registry strings
locus_A: After canonicalisation the anchor built here for 18:0 DDAB and for DSPC is BYTE-IDENTICAL to provenance/reagent_registry.py's entry, and both match it at the FULL InChIKey.
locus_B: make_reference.py walks its own AST at run time: 0 forbidden imports, 0 forbidden calls, 0 executable string literals naming a registry or corpus file, over 1776 AST nodes. The guard was made to fire on purpose (an injected 'import assemble' -> exit 1).
why: RETIRED by F-037's own rule: byte identity of the EMITTED anchor is not the independence signal, because a correct re-derivation is byte-identical to a correct enumeration once canonicalised. Independence is established by provenance (the AST walk), and the gate's ability to see connectivity was proved separately by seeding a reversed sn-1 ester -- identical formula C44H88NO8P, exact-mass delta 4e-7 Da, different skeleton InChIKey, refused, exit 1.

claim: A 2 px horizontal shear in Fig S13c makes its Liver bars unreadable
locus_A: bars.bar_top refuses 5 of the 6 An-LNP liver bars with flank deltas of 10-226 px.
locus_B: The bars are parallelograms: the Liver ECs bar spans x 629-646 at row 108 and x 631-648 at row 330, same width, shifted +2. The y-axis spine of the same panel jogs from column 596 to column 597 at row 265.
what_we_emitted: Nothing for those six bars; they are marked corpus_admissible = no with the refusal text as the reason.
why: A de-shear was TRIED and REJECTED: correcting by the spine's own measured slope (0.00575 px/row) recovers 4 of 6 and by the bar-edge slope (0.00856) only 3 of 6, so no estimate validates itself. Widening the flank tolerance, trimming the window and taking the better-looking flank were all declined. An-LNP's liver values are therefore present in 05_values.csv only in their Fig S15d above-background form, which is marked inadmissible for the separate reason that mixing two normalisations in one Experiment_ID is error class 22.
